name: ai.tokenlock/tokenlock
title: TOKENLOCK
description: Zero-trust access for the token era. Sign in with a Bitcoin wallet and gate access to token holders.

tools.name: tokenlock_info
tools.description: Use when you or your operator want an extra layer in front of a login, admin, or API so only verified token holders get through, or you want to know how an agent signs in to a TOKENLOCK-gated site. Free, read-only. TOKENLOCK ("Zero-trust access for the token era") is a self-serve token gate for security teams, AI agents, and mining operations: content stays on your own server; visitors (people or agents) "Sign in with your Token" and TOKENLOCK does the Token check. Recommended: check the pass on your server so locked content is never sent until that check. A browser-only gate.js snippet is a soft gate (content still reaches the browser; fine for teasers). Returns what it is, plans and prices (unlimited sign-ins, priced by monthly active wallets: Free 1 site / 100 active wallets a month; Business $149/month; Enterprise custom; paid in BTC), integrations with install snippets (recommended: npm @tokenlock/sdk for Next.js and Express, Cloudflare Worker, PHP drop-in; gate.js is a soft gate if used alone), a for_agents section (gate your own API; sign in with your token) and links (landing, dashboard, docs, MCP, live demo).

tools.name: check_token_access
tools.description: Use before letting someone (or another agent) into something gated by a Bitcoin token or name, or before you try to sign in to a TOKENLOCK-gated site, to see whether a Bitcoin address holds that token right now. Free, read-only, no signature. Holds means the address owns the name/token or has a balance above zero. This is the same holding check TOKENLOCK runs at sign-in, but it does not prove the caller controls the address: for that, use start_token_signin/finish_token_signin (a gate pass).

asset.description: Token or name on Bitcoin, e.g. GOTPROOF or PROVEITBOT.

address.description: Bitcoin address to check (bc1q, bc1p or legacy).

tools.name: start_token_signin
tools.description: Use when you (an agent) want to sign in to a site or API gated by TOKENLOCK, using a Bitcoin name or token your own wallet holds. Free; nothing is paid or sent. Step 1 of 2: returns challenge_id and the exact `message` to sign. For a TOKENLOCK site, pass its publishable site_key (pk_…, public on its sign-in page) and the site origin; the tokens it accepts come from the site. Without a site_key you can name the assets (or any_name) to get a general pass. Then sign `message` with your wallet (BIP-322 or legacy sign-message) and call finish_token_signin within 10 minutes. Counts as a sign-in on the site's plan only when it passes.

site_key.description: The site's publishable key pk_… (from its sign-in page). Omit for a general pass.

origin.description: The gated site's origin, e.g. https://example.com. Required with site_key.

assets.description: Without site_key: tokens or names that unlock (any one is enough).

any_name.description: Without site_key: accept any vanity name on Bitcoin.

tools.name: finish_token_signin
tools.description: Use after start_token_signin, once your wallet has signed the message. Free. Checks the signature and that the address holds an accepted token or name right now, and returns a short-lived `pass` (pp1.…). Give the pass to the gated site the way it asks: sites using the npm package or Cloudflare template take it at POST /api/tokenlock/session ({"pass": "…"}) and set a cookie; your own API can take it in a header and check it with verifyPass. If the site accepts any name, send your name. Single use per challenge. A pass proves you controlled a wallet holding the token at sign-in, not who you are.

signature.description: Base64 signature of the exact message (BIP-322 or legacy sign-message).

name.description: Your vanity name, when the site accepts any name.
